issue_plan.name: Complete configured Go runtime acceptance
issue_plan.summary: First add a production Go lifecycle collector and exercise it through the shared acceptance lifecycle with real local Go processes. Then connect the same collector to prepared Docker environments and verify its transport, deadlines and cleanup. Together these issues deliver explicit lower-level base-failure and candidate-success checks while keeping configured factory admission, default registration and compiler-failure qualification disabled. Each issue updates SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and the README adapter status for what it ships; the merger records the missing selection/discovery decision and the new runtime decisions before dependent work proceeds.

issues.title: Collect independent Go runtime evidence through the shared lifecycle
issues.body:
This is the first of two ordered plumbing issues completing #534, the runtime step of #523's ratified Go-adapter plan within #513/#452. The base already contains #527's GoRepositoryAcceptanceAdapter.Select and Discover and #515's shared acceptance lifecycle. Add a production Go runtime collector callable through a trusted host-owned transport boundary, and exercise it through RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance, Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and explicitly configured Sandbox.Run using real local Go processes. This issue must deliver a working local transport fixture calling production selection, discovery and collection; the following issue supplies the prepared-Docker transport for that identical collector.

Execute each acceptance selector separately in its captured owning part's directory using its safely narrowed test_one arguments. Reuse go_acceptance.go and go_discovery.go rather than inventing a second selection/discovery policy. Preserve the complete supported command grammar documented in docs/factory.md, every accepted flag's semantics and argument boundaries, normal production files and dependencies, build constraints, local module ownership and independently escaped/anchored literal selector components. Unsupported commands remain refused before preparation or execution. Runtime collection follows real package loading, source/declaration validation and compilation; discovery alone does not establish that an exact subtest exists. The verbatim acceptance bytes, complete (part, framework, file, selector) identity, discovered import path and captured execution digest stay pinned.

Implement framework-origin start and terminal lifecycle collection with a trusted channel independent of both workload stdout and stderr. Retain enough parent/child lifecycle to validate exactly one requested selection, including an exact nested subtest. A parent, prefix, sibling, another parameter case or a parameterized family cannot stand in for a requested exact child. Bind collected evidence to the host's fresh InvocationID, complete identity, discovered package, SourceDigest and ExecutionDigest before returning it through the existing shared evidence boundary. Any helper or framework hook must come from trusted host code and preserve acceptance source bytes and Go testing semantics. Keep its producer, lifecycle validation and record conversion in production code that the later Docker transport can invoke unchanged. Its dependencies must be satisfied by the pinned Go toolchain and standard library offline; do not require Python, host caches, installation, downloads or network.

Workload output before tests, during initialization, in TestMain and during tests is diagnostics only, even when it contains PASS/FAIL, Go lifecycle lines, test2json JSON, runner records, fresh-looking bindings or framing-looking bytes. Parsing those diagnostics into a new record format does not create independent evidence. A process exit, successful compile, synthetic process-exit failure or fabricated runner marker cannot establish completion. A genuinely completed assertion failure or panic with authentic Go framework failure completion is test/failed. A selected skip is test/skipped and qualifies as neither a candidate pass nor a base failure. Zero-test success, an absent selector or child, TestMain exiting before m.Run, a nonzero abrupt exit, interruption and missing terminal events cannot qualify. Preserve running, refused and unstarted outcomes and explanatory reasons instead of assigning an unattributed exit to a failed test.

Use the existing shared lifecycle and repositoryEvidence validation. Exactly one matching completed selection may qualify; reject duplicate, stale, contradictory, truncated and mismatched evidence, including another file, package, module or part. The Go collector must require authentic start and terminal evidence without imposing new mandatory methods or Go-specific evidence rules on #515's trusted fake adapters. Compiler errors remain setup/refusal outcomes here, even for a proposed API; precise compiler attribution belongs to the already ordered next issue of #523, outside #534. Preserve the existing fake adapters' attributable compile-failure contract. Base checks attempt all independent selectors after ordinary build/suite and completed test failures and need a completed attributable failure for every identity; a mixed pass/fail base cannot qualify by broadcasting the failure. Candidate checks need every applicable captured command and every selector to pass. Setup, discovery, transport, allowance exhaustion, cancellation and failed cleanup veto qualification without erasing earlier completed results. Full identities, kinds, statuses and reasons survive output clipping and JSON transport.

All selection, discovery, compilation, helper preparation, collection and testing consume the inherited twelve-minute whole-run cap and any shorter caller/preparer limits. The first suite test or acceptance discovery/execution starts the one shared ten-minute test-phase cap; another selector or part cannot reset it. Keep private regular-file staging, verbatim sources even after line-ending normalization, verified offline dependencies, one active disposable part environment, bounded uncanceled cleanup and queue ownership through cleanup. Build the transport abstraction with these contexts and cleanup ownership now, so Docker can implement it without a second scheduler or renewed allowances.

Add default Go acceptance/regression tests using small standard-library-only temporary modules and isolated temporary caches, with actual Go package/declaration discovery, compilation, testing and the production collector. No Docker, network or opt-in is allowed for these tests; a fake JSON producer is not a framework-outcome test. Demonstrate a real assertion failing against base production code and passing after only a production-file change, while the acceptance bytes remain identical. Exercise the shared base and candidate paths, ordinary failing suite commands followed by independent acceptance, every applicable candidate-command requirement, and two selected tests in one package where one already passes and the other fails. Include identical names across packages, modules and parts, an external test package, build-tag inclusion/exclusion, exact nested subtests containing regexp punctuation and shell-looking text, prefix/sibling/parameter-case neighbors and absent children. Check that wrong-file, excluded-file and multiple-match discovery refusals prevent runtime attribution.

Exercise real skips, zero-test success, absent selectors, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exit, assertion failures, authentic panic completion and interruption. Print forged lifecycle lines, test2json JSON and runner records, including framing-looking bytes, to BOTH stdout and stderr before AND during tests. Include genuine successful execution with fake failure diagnostics and incomplete execution with fake success and fake failure diagnostics; diagnostics must neither manufacture completion nor override genuine outcomes. Wrap the shared environment's RunAcceptance seam to corrupt otherwise real collected evidence: duplicate selection/start/terminal, stale invocation, conflicting outcomes, truncated/missing completion, wrong identity/package/source/execution bindings, and transport errors, including errors after completed evidence. Compare with uncorrupted real controls and retain earlier completed results when a later selector fails. Observe inherited deadlines and cancellation with bounded real subprocesses, and verify retained identities/reasons after clipping and JSON transport.

Inspect and preserve the existing contracts in internal/plumbing/acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go and acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go. Also inspect go_selection_accept_test.go, go_discovery_accept_test.go, go_discovery_regression_test.go and go_lifecycle_accept_test.go. Their Run/ReadFile/Close-only discovery fixtures deliberately cannot execute tests or supply runtime evidence; keep those controls and add a distinct local runtime transport instead of turning discovery into completion. Preserve native_execution_accept_test.go, the native hash/lock tests and built-in sandbox coverage. Before ratifying this issue's implementation plan, name any existing test file whose fixture/command assumptions actually need changes; the preceding tests are not permission to weaken their assertions.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and README.md's adapter-status sentence in this same pull request to state the implemented lower-level Go runtime API, supported command/selector forms, independent evidence criteria, compiler restriction, and continued factory-admission restriction. At this stage describe the production collector exercised by a local transport and the still-pending prepared-Docker transport accurately; do not claim that Docker already collects evidence. Keep README.md at most 400 lines, with detail in docs/factory.md, and cite existing decisions in each changed SPEC bullet. Leave configured planning admission, default adapter registration, candidate-controlled registration, external plumbing and production pytest/Vitest/Jest disabled. Preserve legacy Go execution, hashes and locks without inferred metadata or migration.

Foundations: D-0105 (tested plumbing), D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, #484/D-0311, #503/D-0314 and #515/D-0316, plus #527's ratified selection/discovery contract. The supplied base has #527's code and SPEC bullet but no corresponding journal decision; merger work must record/confirm that decision and use its real ID, never an invented citation. The merger records this runtime-collection decision before the dependent issue proceeds because a plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Decision recording and genuinely unavailable Docker/network checks belong under Merger work and alone do not require repair; the default real-Go tests above are required, and affected opt-in real Python/TLAPS CI suites remain required.

Kind: plumbing

issues.title: Run Go acceptance in prepared Docker environments
issues.body:
This is the second and final ordered plumbing issue completing #534, the runtime step of #523's ratified Go-adapter plan within #513/#452. It starts only after the preceding issue, Collect independent Go runtime evidence through the shared lifecycle, has merged. That issue supplies the production collector, its trusted transport boundary and default real-Go lifecycle tests. Implement the transport in DockerDependencyRunner.OpenChecks' prepared Go environment so it supplies RepositoryAcceptanceEnvironment.RunAcceptance and real lower-level Go base-failure and candidate-success checks work through Sandbox.checkRepositoryBase and explicitly configured Sandbox.Run in the prepared Docker environment.

Use the preceding issue's identical production producer, parent/child lifecycle collector and evidence validation; do not add a Docker-specific interpretation of Go outcomes or a second diagnostic parser. Reuse #527's GoRepositoryAcceptanceAdapter.Select/Discover and #515's fresh invocation bindings, private source staging and shared lifecycle. Run every acceptance selector separately in its owning part, with the captured safely narrowed test_one command, the complete supported flag policy, literal argument boundaries, build constraints, normal production sources/dependencies and exact literal component selection. Discovery must identify the pinned included declaration and actual package before runtime attribution. Full (part, framework, file, selector) identity, verbatim source digest, captured execution digest, discovered package and fresh host invocation ID must survive transport unchanged. Unsupported commands still stop before preparation/execution; wrong-file, excluded-file and multiple-match discovery cannot produce runtime evidence.

Provide a trusted transport separate from workload stdout and stderr, including output emitted before tests and from initialization and TestMain. Stage any trusted helper and evidence resources under host control, separately from the candidate source tree, and use the existing pinned prepared Go image and its tools. Collection must need no Python, host Go cache, installation, downloads or network. Do not make candidate configuration a source of helper code, commands, registration or transport authority. Transport may carry the collector's authentic framework events/results, never promote captured workload diagnostics into evidence. A process exit, compile success, PASS/FAIL text, test2json-looking JSON, synthetic process-exit failure, framing-looking bytes or a fabricated runner marker is insufficient.

Retain exactly-one completed-selection semantics, actual start and terminal events and enough parent/child lifecycle to distinguish the requested exact subtest from its parent, siblings and parameter family. Completed assertion failures and panics with authentic framework failure completion are test/failed; selected skips are test/skipped and satisfy neither candidate nor base. Zero-test success, absent selectors/children, TestMain exit before m.Run, nonzero abrupt exits, interrupted processes and missing terminal events remain nonqualifying with useful running/refused/unstarted statuses. Duplicate, stale, conflicting, truncated or wrong-binding records and transport failures veto qualification. Keep earlier completed results and full identities, kinds, statuses and reasons through output clipping and JSON transport. Compiler failures remain nonqualifying setup/refusal outcomes until the next separately ordered #523 compiler-attribution issue.

Preserve the actual prepared-container contract: a verified immutable dependency image, network none, pull never, pinned platform, overridden entrypoint, explicit clean environment with proxy defaults suppressed, init, 4 GiB and 1,024 processes, owning-part working directory, offline verified dependencies and no host mounts. Retain GOPROXY=off, GOSUMDB=off, GOTOOLCHAIN=local, GOENV=off, GOWORK=off, captured readonly/vendor policy and disposable build caches. Literal selectors, including shell syntax, must remain arguments rather than wrapper source. One part keeps one active disposable environment across its captured commands and selectors; another part starts only after that environment is cleaned up. Existing Run, ReadFile and Close calls and non-Go suite environments retain their behavior.

Everything including helper staging/building, discovery, compilation, event transport and testing uses the original twelve-minute whole-run limit, shortened by the caller and preparer. The first suite test or acceptance starts the shared ten-minute phase; later selectors, parts and setup consume its remainder without resetting it. Preserve the existing startup/cleanup reserves and bounded uncanceled cleanup after success, failed startup, command failure, evidence failure or cancellation. Join or terminate owned processes/transports, remove container and private staging, and hold queue ownership until cleanup ends. A setup, discovery, transport, timeout, interruption or cleanup failure vetoes base and candidate qualification while preserving earlier completed work. Base checks continue independent selectors after ordinary suite/test failures; candidates still require every applicable captured command and all selectors to pass.

Add default tests of the production Docker invocation and transport construction without requiring a Docker daemon or network. Replace only the Docker process/transport boundary, inspect the actual create/copy/start/exec/read/cleanup calls and argument vectors, and exercise the production wrapper's literal forwarding where possible. Verify the prepared image ID, owning directory, isolation flags, explicit offline environment, proxy suppression, no pull/build/commit or installation during checks, no host mounts/cache/Python, one active part environment and cleanup ordering. Test transport setup/read failures, malformed/truncated transport, cancellation and cleanup failure with retained partial results. Any existing fake that validates command lines, flags, copy archives or output must keep its original assertions while accommodating explicitly authorized new runtime transport calls.

Inspect internal/plumbing/repository_container_accept_test.go (docker484 logs NUL-separated argv, supplies diagnostic exec output and checks the four ordinary suite calls), repository_execution_regression_test.go (executes the captured env/positional-shell wrapper), repository_sandbox_accept_test.go (persistent environment, captured policy, deadlines and partial work), go_container_accept_test.go (source archive and exact selected arguments) and go_discovery_regression_test.go (unsafe source archives). Prefer a separate runtime Docker fixture or optional new fixture behavior so existing suite/discovery calls retain their current contracts; name every existing test file that needs modification in this issue's implementation plan. Preserve acceptance_lifecycle_accept_test.go, acceptance_evidence_accept_test.go, acceptance_budget_accept_test.go, acceptance_foundation_regression_test.go and acceptance_interruption_regression_test.go's trusted fake-adapter contracts, native_execution_accept_test.go, and built-in sandbox coverage.

Keep the default real-Go tests from the predecessor mandatory. Extend them through the same transport abstraction now used by Docker, so production selection, discovery and the identical collector still execute real standard-library Go modules without Docker/network. Do not replace any framework outcome with canned JSON. Demonstrate base failure and candidate success after only a production change with identical acceptance bytes, mixed passing/failing selectors in one package, exact child selection and cross-package/module/part identity. Retain real skip/zero-test/TestMain-exit/abrupt-exit/assertion/panic/interruption cases and forged lifecycle, JSON, runner and framing bytes on both streams before and during execution. Corrupt otherwise real evidence only at the shared environment fault-injection seam for duplicates, stale/conflicting/truncated/wrong-binding records and transport failures. Add real-collector lifecycle coverage for shorter caller/preparer budgets, suite-started and acceptance-started phase deadlines, later-part setup, cancellation during execution/cleanup, queue ownership through cleanup and structured JSON results. Fake-container tests establish Docker construction, not Go framework outcomes.

Add a documented opt-in prepared-image smoke test for behavior a transport fake cannot establish: run the actual production Docker environment and collector offline in the pinned Go image, demonstrating a real base assertion failure, the same acceptance passing after a production fix, an exact child, skip/abrupt-exit nonqualification and diagnostic-forgery resistance. Use an already prepared/available immutable image and report missing Docker/image prerequisites clearly rather than downloading during the check. Unavailable Docker/network may defer this real-image check to Merger work; it must not replace the mandatory default real-Go suite or the daemon-free Docker-boundary tests.

Update SPEC.md, docs/factory.md and the README adapter-status sentence in this pull request to describe the now-working lower-level production Go runtime API including prepared Docker, supported forms and independent evidence requirements, the compiler-attribution restriction and the continuing factory-admission restriction. Cite existing decisions in changed SPEC bullets; use docs/factory.md for detail and keep README.md at most 400 lines. Do not enable default adapters, configured factory planning, candidate-controlled registration, external plumbing or production pytest/Vitest/Jest. Preserve legacy Go execution, hashes and locks without inferred metadata or migration. This completes #534's runtime scope; leave no runtime transport, lifecycle validation or required default tests for an unplanned follow-up.

Foundations: D-0105, D-0107, D-0108, D-0110, D-0111, D-0121, D-0122, D-0173, D-0281, D-0282, D-0294, D-0301, D-0305, #484/D-0311, #503/D-0314 and #515/D-0316, plus the recorded #527 selection/discovery decision and the preceding collector issue's decision. The merger records the completed adapter-execution decision before #523's compiler-attribution issue proceeds; this plumbing build cannot write decisions/. Decision recording and unavailable Docker/network checks are Merger work, not repair requirements on their own. Affected opt-in real Python and TLAPS suites remain required in CI.

Kind: plumbing
